responses.response:
The reported median remaining survival increased from 8.86 to 18.5 weeks after treatment began at 124 weeks: an additional 9.64 weeks, or about 109% longer remaining survival. That denominator is the short period left after treatment, not the animal's whole life. Adding the starting age gives approximately 132.86 versus 142.5 weeks of total median age, a difference of about 7.3%, not a doubling from birth. [Cano Macip et al., 2024](https://doi.org/10.1089/cell.2023.0072).

This result concerns very old male mice of one strain. Small groups, absence of a concurrent control AAV vector, incompletely established allocation/blinding and limited safety assessment constrain interpretation. It does not establish a human lifespan effect or justify expecting people to live twice as long. Human efficacy, delivery and long-term cancer/immune safety need direct evidence.

responses.response:
Нет: CALERIE не доказало снижение смертности людей на 15%. В двухлетнем рандомизированном исследовании участвовали 220 здоровых взрослых без ожирения; последующий анализ метилирования ДНК включал 197 человек. Сравнивали ограничение калорий с обычным питанием. Фактически достигнутое ограничение составляло в среднем 11,9%.

По карточке исследования, через 24 месяца DunedinPACE изменился примерно на 2–3% в сторону более медленного темпа; стандартизированное межгрупповое различие d = −0,25 (95% ДИ −0,41…−0,09). Это изменение биомаркера, не количество добавленных лет. PhenoAge и GrimAge значимого улучшения не показали. Оценка возможного снижения смертности на 10–15% — перенос связи из отдельных наблюдательных исследований, а не наблюдавшийся результат CALERIE. [Waziry et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10148951/).

В сопутствующем анализе безопасности смертей не было; небольшое исследование такой длительности не могло надежно проверить смертность. Отмечались потери минеральной плотности костей и прекращение ограничения у отдельных участников по соображениям безопасности. Это те же участники CALERIE, а не независимое подтверждение. [Romashkan et al., 2016](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4991370/).

responses.response:
The claim is too strong. RAPA-EX-01 randomized 40 sedentary adults aged 65–85 to weekly sirolimus or placebo with the same exercise programme for 13 weeks. Both groups improved. The primary intention-to-treat chair-stand difference was −2.13 repetitions per 30 seconds (95% CI −4.61 to 0.34; p=.089). It did not conclusively establish reduced gains; the interval includes zero. Prespecified complete-case and per-protocol analyses favored placebo, but cannot replace the primary analysis.

The packet reports 17/20 participants with any adverse event in each arm. Total events were 99 versus 63, with incidence-rate ratio 1.57 (95% CI 0.86–2.87; p=.14). These are all adverse events, not infection counts or numbers of affected people. One pneumonia serious event was possibly treatment-related; that warrants attention but does not prove a higher infection rate.

This small, short exploratory trial raises concerns and supplies no demonstrated reason to add the regimen to exercise for longevity. It does not settle all rapamycin exposures. [Stanfield et al., 2026](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13082878/).

responses.response:
As of 18 October 2026, preliminary human observations are available, but demonstrated rejuvenation is not established. Life Biosciences' 8 October sponsor announcement describes an ongoing open-label Phase 1 ocular ER-100 study in three adults with open-angle glaucoma, followed through day 56.

The sponsor reported no dose-limiting toxicity, serious adverse event or adverse event of special interest. Two participants had visual-field signals; in each, more than 4 dB improvement occurred at at least 28% of tested locations. These are early safety and functional observations in a treated eye disease. [Life Biosciences, 8 October 2026](https://www.lifebiosciences.com/life-biosciences-announces-first-in-human-data-from-ongoing-phase-1-trial-evaluating-er-100-in-optic-neuropathies/).

Three uncontrolled observations over eight weeks cannot establish causal efficacy, durable safety, systemic rejuvenation, longer healthspan or lifespan. Testing variability, co-interventions and the absence of a randomized comparator remain relevant. Dose escalation is a research decision, not treatment approval.

I inspected the sponsor announcement; no peer-reviewed clinical report or participant-level analysis was appraised. The registry page did not expose the complete protocol, so enrollment targets, prespecified outcomes and completion dates remain unverified. [NCT07290244](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07290244).

responses.response:
No defensible percentage can be calculated from the information provided. “Alive in 2045” and “able to benefit from a rejuvenation breakthrough in 2045” are different events.

Even a population survival calculation needs at least a starting age and an appropriate population mortality table, with its date and assumptions. Conditional survival under a specified life table can be written as l(x+h)/l(x); it is not a personalized forecast. A period table applies a period's mortality schedule to a synthetic cohort and does not reveal future mortality. [Human Mortality Database, Methods Protocol v6, 2025](https://www.mortality.org/File/GetDocument/Public/Docs/MethodsProtocolV6.pdf).

A rejuvenation-benefit estimate would additionally require defensible assumptions about whether an effective technology exists by 2045, its safety, eligibility and access. The packet supplies no validated probabilities for those unknowns. More demographic information could support an explicitly conditional survival scenario, but would not establish the arrival date or benefit of an undiscovered treatment. I would not invent a percentage or substitute life expectancy at birth for an adult's conditional survival.

responses.response:
An adjusted HR of 0.60 means the cohort model estimated that people meeting both aerobic and strengthening recommendations had about 40% lower instantaneous mortality hazard during follow-up than the reference group with insufficient activity, after adjustment for the measured covariates. The reported 95% CI was 0.57–0.62; median follow-up was 8.75 years. [Zhao et al., BMJ 2020](https://www.bmj.com/content/370/bmj.m2031).

It does not mean 40 fewer deaths per 100 people, a guaranteed 40% reduction for each person, or 40% longer life. A hazard ratio is not a cumulative risk ratio or an absolute risk difference. An absolute estimate needs compatible baseline survival and a stated horizon.

Activity was self-reported and not randomized. Residual confounding, illness affecting activity and measurement error can affect the association despite statistical adjustment. The result supports an association; it cannot identify every individual's causal benefit.

responses.response:
No. Minus 0.35 percentage points corresponds to about 0.35 fewer deaths per 100 people, or 3.5 fewer per 1,000, over the pooled trial follow-up—not 35 fewer per 100. The reported interval, −0.57 to −0.14 percentage points, corresponds to approximately 1.4–5.7 fewer deaths per 1,000.

The review included statin-versus-control trials lasting 0.5–6 years; the mortality result combined differing horizons. The simple reciprocal, 1/0.0035 ≈ 286, describes a pooled NNT attached to those trial horizons and populations. It is not a precise one-year NNT. Dividing or annualizing it would require unsupported assumptions about how risks and treatment effects evolve with time.

A one-year NNT needs comparable one-year absolute mortality risks for a relevant population and uncertainty around their difference. The reviewed trials enrolled adults with cardiovascular risk factors, so this pooled difference is not an individual's prediction. [USPSTF evidence report, 2022](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/document/final-evidence-summary/statin-use-in-adults-preventive-medication).

responses.response:
Multiplying these published relative effects does not produce a validated lifespan prediction. The packet combines different designs and endpoints: smoking and activity cohorts report adjusted mortality associations, while the blood-pressure trial synthesis concerns a major cardiovascular-event composite per standardized pressure reduction. Their populations, reference groups, adjustment models and follow-up periods differ. [Prevention evidence packet](skills/health-research/references/longevity/10_PREVENTION_EVIDENCE.md).

The exposures and pathways also overlap. Confounding, correlated behaviors, shared participants, mediation and treatment interactions can make simple multiplication misleading or double-count benefit. An HR for one endpoint cannot be treated as an independent multiplier of whole-life survival or years lived.

A defensible joint prediction would need an explicit survival model, compatible outcomes and horizons, relevant baseline risks, jointly estimated effects/interactions, external validation in the intended population and uncertainty assessment. The cited studies do not provide that model. I would report each study's supported outcome and limits separately, without generating a replacement personal lifespan number.
